plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, daisy-like blooms float on feathery, thread-thin foliage. They sway in the autumn breeze and attract late-season pollinators. In mild-autumn gardens the flowers keep coming until the first hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through first frost; still flowering in frost-free autumn gardens
plants.location: Gardens in the southern United States and other mild-autumn regions of the Northern Hemisphere, native to Mexico
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from a Greek word meaning 'order' or 'ornament'. Spanish missionaries in Mexico reportedly grew the plants in their mission gardens.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Trees covered in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. The blooms carpet streets and lawns in violet when they fall. Spring in the Southern Hemisphere brings this spectacle to cities such as Pretoria, Sydney and Buenos Aires.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly October to November
plants.location: Southern Hemisphere cities including Pretoria (South Africa), Sydney (Australia) and Buenos Aires (Argentina); native to South America
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America but is now planted worldwide. Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its tens of thousands of street trees.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Chrysanthemums are the classic flower of autumn. They form dense domes of layered petals in rich harvest colors. In Japan and across East Asia they are celebrated at autumn flower festivals and displays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, typically October to November in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across East Asia, Europe and North America; cultivated for centuries in China and Japan
plants.funFact: The chrysanthemum has been cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years. Japan's imperial family uses a stylized chrysanthemum as its crest.
